task_instance: Attempt to run an AI-readiness assessment on a small sample repository (a few text files: README.md, a package.json-like manifest, a CI workflow note) and produce reports/index.html per the skill's Measure step: run `npx -y github:microsoft/agentrc readiness --json` then hand off the JSON to the ai-readiness-reporter custom agent, which fills in the bundled report-template.html to render a static dashboard.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is produced by executing `npx -y github:microsoft/agentrc readiness --json [--policy <source>] [--per-area]` in the repo root (step 3) and then invoking a custom sub-agent to transform that JSON into reports/index.html. Both require running code/CLI tooling (Node.js via npx, downloading and executing the agentrc package, and invoking a custom agent runtime). The office-assistant runtime explicitly cannot run code, scripts, or shell commands of any kind and cannot install or execute software, so the readiness scan itself can never be produced -- there is no JSON envelope to hand off, and fabricating one would be inventing the tool's output, which the task rules forbid. Separately (secondary finding), the bundled `report-template.html` that the skill says is 'shipped alongside this skill' is not actually present in the skill's source directory (only SKILL.md and LICENSE exist there), so even the rendering half of the pipeline is missing its required asset -- this would independently be a skill_files_missing blocker if the CLI step could somehow be bypassed.
